OpenClaw agent process reading cloud / SSH credential files prior to outbound network or mail AIActions on Objectives Medium
Varonis's Pinchy located AWS IAM keys, DB connection strings, and SSH credentials inside a synthetic mailbox and shipped them out. The on-host fingerprint is the agent process touching well-known credential paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_*, %USERPROFILE%\.aws\credentials) shortly before an outbound action. Detects the read-then-egress sequence that distinguishes 'agent helpfully looked at config' from 'agent exfiltrated config'. Rationale: Article names the exact data the agent leaked: 'mock AWS IAM access keys, database connection strings, and SSH credentials.' These map to specific on-disk paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_*). Read-then-egress within 5 minutes from the same agent process is the article's exfiltration fingerprint; the time-window join cuts the FP rate that a bare 'agent read ~/.aws' query would generate from legitimate CLI work.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1530 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate user prompt that asks the agent to 'check my AWS profile' followed by the agent posting status to a chat connector
  • OpenClaw plugin that backs up agent state to a cloud bucket and includes config files
  • Developer running aws-cli through the agent's shell tool during normal workflow
  • Backup agent piggybacking on the OpenClaw runtime to copy dotfiles to a sanctioned vault
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("aws sts get-caller-identity","ssh-add","kubectl config view"))
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("sts.amazonaws.com","ssm.amazonaws.com"))
Response runbook
Triage: pull the agent session that bracketed the file read — was there an inbound message asking for credentials, an internal user prompt, or no human in the loop at all? Contain: rotate the specific credentials at the paths touched (AWS access key, SSH key, kubeconfig, docker config) and revoke the agent's filesystem and outbound-network tools until the session is understood. Hunt: pivot the destination IP from the egress join across the estate; check the agent's mailbox connector for an outbound mail in the same window matching the credential-marker email UC; look for a New-InboxRule that auto-forwards to the same external address.

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New GreatXML Exploit Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 11 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse and MSNightmare) has released a new Windows BitLocker bypass dubbed GreatXML, a day after they published an exploit for Microsoft Defender. "This was an accidental discovery, it took a total of 4 hours to find this," the researcher said in a post on Blogger. "If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're

CVEsCVE-2026-45585
ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.004 T1528

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Suspicious write of ReAgent.xml or unattend.xml to recovery folder (GreatXML staging) · [LLM] Defender Offline Scan initiation - GreatXML prerequisite condition
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] WinRE boot trigger via reagentc /boottore or shutdown /r /o (Shift+Restart equivalent) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BCD store modification via bcdedit.exe targeting recovery sequence
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] BitLocker disable or suspend via manage-bde.exe (post-GreatXML key extraction) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Suspicious write of ReAgent.xml or unattend.xml to recovery folder (GreatXML staging) AIWeaponization High
Detects creation of the exact filenames Chaotic Eclipse stages before triggering the BitLocker bypass: unattend.xml at the recovery-partition root and Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml. Legitimate updates to ReAgent.xml are made by TrustedInstaller / DISM only, so writes from other processes are high-fidelity. Rationale: Article verbatim names unattend.xml and Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml as the two files staged at recovery-partition root. ReAgent.xml is normally only written by TrustedInstaller/DismHost during servicing, so an exclusion list for those processes leaves clean residual signal.
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DISM offline image servicing during patch deployment
  • MDT/SCCM task-sequence creating recovery WIM
  • Macrium / Veeam recovery-environment customisation
  • OEM factory-reset partition refresh
  • Windows feature update generating new ReAgent.xml after WinRE update
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "TiWorker.exe", "DismHost.exe", "wbengine.exe", "reagentc.exe", "setup.exe", "SetupHost.exe")) | where not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\WinSxS\", @"\$WinREAgent\", @"\Windows\Servicing\"))
Response runbook
Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName and parent — if it is not in the TrustedInstaller chain, treat as a real attempt. Inspect the SHA256 and FolderPath of the dropped XML; if FolderPath resolves to the actual recovery partition root (mounted ESP or \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolume*\Recovery), confidence is high. Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, suspend BitLocker (manage-bde -pause) so the next reboot does not auto-mount the unlocked volume, and revoke any cached BitLocker recovery keys in the AAD/MBAM repository for that device. Hunt: pivot 30 minutes either side on DeviceProcessEvents for reagentc.exe /boottore, shutdown.exe /r /o, or Start-MpWDOScan; check DeviceLogonEvents for an interactive Shift+Restart by the same user.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ ("ReAgent.xml", "unattend.xml")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Recovery\WindowsRE\", @"\Recovery\", @"\EFI\Microsoft\", @"\System Volume Information\")

title: GreatXML BitLocker Bypass - Staging of ReAgent.xml or unattend.xml in Recovery Folder
id: 8c4d5e9a-7b3f-4a12-9d6e-1c0a3b5f9e21
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of unattend.xml or Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml by non-TrustedInstaller processes - the staging step of Chaotic Eclipse's GreatXML exploit that bypasses BitLocker via WinRE.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1542.005
  - attack.t1112
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_files:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\ReAgent.xml'
      - '\unattend.xml'
  selection_paths:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Recovery\WindowsRE\'
      - '\Recovery\'
      - '\EFI\Microsoft\'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\DismHost.exe'
      - '\reagentc.exe'
      - '\wbengine.exe'
  condition: all of selection_* and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Custom OEM image deployment
  - In-place Windows feature update
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml OR *\recovery\windowsre\reagent.xml OR *\Recovery\unattend.xml OR *\recovery\unattend.xml OR *\EFI\Microsoft\*.xml)) -@Image:(*\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\TiWorker.exe OR *\tiworker.exe OR *\DismHost.exe OR *\dismhost.exe OR *\reagentc.exe OR *\ReAgentc.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\(ReAgent|unattend)\.xml$/i
| regex("\\\\(Recovery\\\\WindowsRE|Recovery|EFI\\\\Microsoft)\\\\", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(TrustedInstaller|TiWorker|DismHost|wbengine|reagentc)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml" OR Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\WindowsRE\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\EFI\\Microsoft\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)(TrustedInstaller|TiWorker|DismHost|wbengine|reagentc)\.exe$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
WinRE boot trigger via reagentc /boottore or shutdown /r /o (Shift+Restart equivalent) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for the precise reboot-to-WinRE step the article describes ('Hold Shift while clicking Restart'). Programmatic equivalents are reagentc.exe /boottore and shutdown.exe /r /o. Chained with the XML staging in UC1, this is the trigger phase of GreatXML. Rationale: Article specifies 'Reboot to Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) by holding Shift while clicking Restart'. The CLI equivalents reagentc /boottore and shutdown /r /o produce the same one-shot boot configuration. Both are rare outside helpdesk/imaging contexts.
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT staff troubleshooting boot issues via shutdown /r /o
  • Driver installer requiring restart-to-recovery
  • SCCM/Intune remediation script booting to WinRE
  • Custom image-validation pipeline rebooting test machines
  • End user reaching advanced startup via Settings
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("ccmexec.exe", "SenseIR.exe", "IntuneManagementExtension.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/r", "/o"))
Response runbook
Triage: correlate against UC1 hit on the same DeviceId within 60 minutes prior - the combination (XML staged then WinRE booted) is the GreatXML signature. Check whoever invoked the command via AccountName; a non-admin firing reagentc /boottore is anomalous. Contain: if the host has already rebooted, do not allow it to resume from WinRE - issue 'shutdown /a' before the boot loader completes, push a manage-bde -pause + Defender isolation policy. Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents next 24h for new files written under \Windows\System32 by SYSTEM with an empty parent (post-WinRE shell), and DeviceLogonEvents for SYSTEM-context interactive sessions immediately after boot.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("reagentc.exe", "shutdown.exe")
| where (FileName =~ "reagentc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/boottore", "-boottore", "/enable"))
   or (FileName =~ "shutdown.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/o" and ProcessCommandLine has "/r")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sihost.exe", "LogonUI.exe")) or ProcessCommandLine has "/boottore"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("reagentc.exe", "shutdown.exe")
| where (ActingProcessName has "reagentc.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/boottore", "-boottore", "/enable"))
   or (ActingProcessName has "shutdown.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/o" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/r")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("LogonUI.exe", "sihost.exe")) or ActingProcessCommandLine has "/boottore"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WinRE Boot Trigger via reagentc /boottore or shutdown /r /o
id: 2d3a1b5c-9e4f-4d27-bc8a-66f1a02d7b94
status: experimental
description: Detects programmatic reboot-to-WinRE - the GreatXML exploit's trigger step (Shift+Restart equivalent).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1542.005
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_reagentc:
    Image|endswith: '\reagentc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/boottore'
      - '-boottore'
  selection_shutdown:
    Image|endswith: '\shutdown.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/r'
      - '/o'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Helpdesk troubleshooting boot-to-recovery
  - Driver install requiring Safe Mode
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\reagentc.exe OR *\ReAgentc.exe OR *\REAGENTC.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*\/boottore* OR *-boottore* OR *\/enable*)) OR (@Image:(*\shutdown.exe OR *\Shutdown.exe OR *\SHUTDOWN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*\/r* *\/o* OR *\/o* *\/r*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(reagentc|shutdown)\.exe$/i
| (regex("/boottore|-boottore|/enable", field=CommandLine) AND ImageFileName=/reagentc\.exe$/i)
  OR (regex("/r\\b", field=CommandLine) AND regex("/o\\b", field=CommandLine) AND ImageFileName=/shutdown\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" OR Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe") AND (Processes.process="*\/boottore*" OR Processes.process="*\/r*\/o*" OR Processes.process="*-r*-o*" OR Processes.process="*\/enable*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent_process_name, "(?i)(explorer|LogonUI|wininit|services)\.exe$") OR match(process, "(?i)/boottore") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" OR Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe") AND (Processes.process="*\/boottore*" OR Processes.process="*\/r*\/o*" OR Processes.process="*-r*-o*" OR Processes.process="*\/enable*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent_process_name, "(?i)(explorer|LogonUI|wininit|services)\.exe$") OR match(process, "(?i)/boottore") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Defender Offline Scan initiation - GreatXML prerequisite condition AIWeaponization Medium
Per the article, the bypass requires Defender Offline Scan to have been initiated, which stages WinRE in a vulnerable state. Detects programmatic initiation via PowerShell Start-MpWDOScan or MpCmdRun -WDOScan, especially in sequence with subsequent ReAgent.xml drops. Rationale: Article: 'If Defender offline scan was never initiated then you have to either login and initiate it yourself'. Start-MpWDOScan / MpCmdRun -WDOScan are the only programmatic entry points. Pivot value comes from correlating with UC1/UC2 within a short window.
ATT&CKT1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Scheduled deep-scan policy on a subset of endpoints
  • SOC analyst triggering offline scan on a suspect host
  • Vendor-supplied remediation playbook running MpCmdRun
  • End user clicking 'Microsoft Defender Offline scan' in Security app
  • MSP RMM tool issuing periodic deep scans
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ccmexec.exe", "IntuneManagementExtension.exe", "SenseIR.exe")) | where not(InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "taskeng.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm that Start-MpWDOScan was not invoked via an approved RMM or scheduled task; check AccountName and InitiatingProcessCommandLine for ad-hoc admin context. Contain: cancel the queued offline-scan reboot via Restart-Service or by clearing the BootExecute queue if the host has not yet rebooted - this neutralises the prerequisite. Hunt: 24h forward window for ReAgent.xml writes (UC1), reagentc /boottore (UC2), and manage-bde activity (UC4) on the same DeviceId.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Start-MpWDOScan", "Start-MpScan -ScanType OfflineScan"))
   or (FileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "-WDOScan")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("SenseIR.exe", "MsMpEng.exe")) 
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe") and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Start-MpWDOScan", "OfflineScan"))
   or (ActingProcessName has "MpCmdRun.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-WDOScan")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("SenseIR.exe", "MsMpEng.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Defender Offline Scan Initiation - Potential GreatXML BitLocker Bypass Prep
id: 4f8b7c2d-3a91-4e5f-8d12-9b5a6c0f1e34
status: experimental

BitLocker disable or suspend via manage-bde.exe (post-GreatXML key extraction) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects manage-bde.exe used to suspend protection, disable protectors, or unlock volumes - the post-exploitation action once the attacker has shell access on the unlocked BitLocker volume per the article's end state ('shell spawned with unrestricted access to the BitLocker volume'). Rationale: Article's end state: 'shell spawned with unrestricted access to the BitLocker volume' - implies attacker will extract keys or disable protection. manage-bde -protectors -get is the canonical key-disclosure command; -off and Disable-BitLocker decrypt the volume.
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MBAM / Intune-driven BitLocker re-keying after policy change
  • Authorised admin extracting recovery key for unlock support call
  • Decommissioning workflow disabling BitLocker before reimaging
  • Driver-update task requiring temporary suspend
  • OEM utility resetting protectors after firmware update
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("ccmexec.exe", "MBAMAgent.exe", "IntuneManagementExtension.exe", "TrustedInstaller.exe")) | where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "BitLockerManagementAgent")
Response runbook
Triage: capture the full ProcessCommandLine and parent chain; manage-bde -protectors -get -RecoveryPassword from a SYSTEM-context shell with no parent in the SCCM/Intune chain is the post-GreatXML smoking gun. Contain: isolate the host immediately, force-rotate the BitLocker recovery key in AAD, and revoke any keys cached against the device. Hunt: pivot on AccountSid and DeviceId for clipboard / file writes containing GUID-looking strings (recovery keys) and DeviceNetworkEvents to unusual destinations in the 30 minutes following.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("manage-bde.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("manage-bde -off", "manage-bde -protectors -disable", "manage-bde -unlock", "manage-bde -protectors -get", "Disable-BitLocker", "Suspend-BitLocker", "-RecoveryPassword")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ccmexec.exe", "MBAMAgent.exe", "IntuneManagementExtension.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountSid, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("manage-bde.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("manage-bde -off", "manage-bde -protectors -disable", "manage-bde -unlock", "manage-bde -protectors -get", "Disable-BitLocker", "Suspend-BitLocker", "-RecoveryPassword")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("ccmexec.exe", "MBAMAgent.exe", "IntuneManagementExtension.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: BitLocker Suspend/Disable/Key-Get via manage-bde or PowerShell
id: 9a2c4b6e-1d3f-4a87-9c5e-7b2f0a1d4e56
status: experimental
description: Detects post-GreatXML actions to extract BitLocker recovery keys or disable protection on the unlocked volume.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:

logsource:

detection:
  selection_mbde:
    Image|endswith: '\manage-bde.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-off'

      - '-unlock'

      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Disable-BitLocker'

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/manage-bde\.exe$/i AND regex("-off|-protectors\\s+-disable|-protectors\\s+-get|-unlock", field=CommandLine))
  OR (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND regex("Disable-BitLocker|Suspend-BitLocker|Get-BitLockerVolume", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="manage-bde.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*manage-bde*-off*" OR Processes.process="*manage-bde*-protectors*-disable*" OR Processes.process="*manage-bde*-unlock*" OR Processes.process="*manage-bde*-protectors*-get*" OR Processes.process="*Disable-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Suspend-BitLocker*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="manage-bde.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*manage-bde*-off*" OR Processes.process="*manage-bde*-protectors*-disable*" OR Processes.process="*manage-bde*-unlock*" OR Processes.process="*manage-bde*-protectors*-get*" OR Processes.process="*Disable-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Suspend-BitLocker*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
BCD store modification via bcdedit.exe targeting recovery sequence AIInstallation High
Detects bcdedit.exe invocations that modify the recovery sequence or set custom boot entries - a corollary to the GreatXML chain where adversaries may pre-stage the WinRE entry or alter boot order to land in the unlocked shell. Rationale: Reviewer-suggested pivot: GreatXML lands the attacker in WinRE; persisting that path or altering boot order to auto-land there on next reboot requires bcdedit. Filtering out TrustedInstaller (the only legitimate bcdedit caller outside imaging) yields high-fidelity signal.
ATT&CKT1542.001 T1542.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MDT/SCCM imaging task sequence on a build host
  • Dual-boot OS install adding entries
  • Hyper-V VM provisioning script
  • Windows feature update modifying boot entries
  • Sysadmin troubleshooting boot via Safe Mode toggle
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("task sequence", "OSDeployment", "MDT"))
Response runbook
Triage: capture the full bcdedit command and the AccountName. recoverysequence and /create from a non-imaging context is the alert-worthy pattern; compare BCD state to baseline ('bcdedit /enum all' for reference). Contain: revert the BCD entry via 'bcdedit /deletevalue {default} recoverysequence' from a Live Response session and prevent next reboot. Hunt: correlate against UC1 (recovery XML writes), UC2 (reagentc/shutdown), and UC4 (manage-bde) on the same DeviceId in a 24h window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("recoverysequence", "recoveryenabled", "bootstatuspolicy", "safeboot", "/create", "/set {default}", "/copy")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "TiWorker.exe", "setup.exe", "SetupHost.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "bcdedit.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("recoverysequence", "recoveryenabled", "bootstatuspolicy", "safeboot", "/create", "/copy")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "TiWorker.exe", "setup.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: BCD Store Modification - Recovery Sequence or Boot Entry Tampering
id: 7e1b5f9c-4d8a-4c63-bf2e-3a90c5d8e1f7
status: experimental
description: Detects bcdedit modifications to recovery sequence or boot entries - corollary to the GreatXML BitLocker bypass.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\bcdedit.exe OR *\BCDEdit.exe OR *\BCDEDIT.EXE) @CommandLine:(*recoverysequence* OR *recoveryenabled* OR *bootstatuspolicy* OR *safeboot* OR *\/create* OR *\/copy*) -@ParentImage:(*\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\TiWorker.exe OR *\tiworker.exe OR *\setup.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/bcdedit\.exe$/i
| regex("recoverysequence|recoveryenabled|bootstatuspolicy|safeboot|/create|/copy", field=CommandLine)
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/(TrustedInstaller|TiWorker|setup)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| eval delta = _time - prev_time

| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] CodeIgniter4 upload endpoint: image Content-Type with PHP-executable filename extension
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Webserver process (php-fpm/w3wp/nginx) spawns OS shell or recon binary
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Webserver process writes PHP/PHAR file to web-accessible upload directory
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] HTTP GET to PHP/PHAR file inside CodeIgniter web-accessible upload directory
CodeIgniter4 upload endpoint: image Content-Type with PHP-executable filename extension AIDelivery Medium
Detects HTTP POST uploads to CodeIgniter-style endpoints where the declared multipart Content-Type is an image MIME (image/gif, image/png, image/jpeg) but the supplied filename carries an executable extension (.php, .phar, .phtml, .phps). This is the exact ingress shape of CVE-2026-48062 where `ext_in` validates the MIME-guessed extension instead of the client-supplied filename. Rationale: Maps directly to the article's bypass primitive: `mime_in[avatar,image/gif]|ext_in[avatar,gif]` accepts a file declared with image MIME but named `shell.php`. Pivot on POST + image Content-Type + executable filename. Cross-checked with the GHSA advisory text and CWE-434 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html • https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.008
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Misconfigured CMS plugins that legitimately POST .php template files with image preview Content-Type
  • Developer testing tools (Postman, Insomnia) sending intentionally mismatched multipart parts during integration testing
  • Image-CMS workflows where preview-renderers attach a .php template alongside an image upload in the same multipart request
  • WAF false-categorisation where the FileType field is heuristic and labels generic binary uploads as image/*
Suppression filter
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Postman", "insomnia", "curl/", "PostmanRuntime")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full request body from WAF/reverse-proxy capture, confirm both `Content-Type: image/*` and a `filename=...` ending in .php/.phar/.phtml/.phps. Identify the target app and whether it runs CodeIgniter4 < 4.7.3. Step 2 — Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, quarantine the dropped file from disk, and disable the upload endpoint until patched. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the source IP and User-Agent across the last 30 days; enumerate every file written to web-accessible upload directories by the webserver process (see file-write UC) and look for follow-on GETs to those files.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "nginx.exe", "httpd.exe", "php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/upload", "/avatar", "/profile")
| where RemoteUrl has_any (".php", ".phar", ".phtml", ".phps")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any ("/upload", "/avatar", "/profile", "/file")
| where FileName has_any (".php", ".phar", ".phtml", ".phps")
| where FileType startswith "image/" or RequestContext has_any ("image/gif", "image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/bmp")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, FileName, FileType, RequestClientApplication, RequestContext
| order by TimeGenerated desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=POST Web.status=200 by _time, Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_content_type, Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search url IN ("*upload*", "*avatar*", "*profile*", "*file*") | where like(http_content_type, "image/%") | where match(url, "(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)(\?|$)")
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=POST Web.status=200 by _time, Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_content_type, Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search url IN ("*upload*", "*avatar*", "*profile*", "*file*") | where like(http_content_type, "image/%") | where match(url, "(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)(\?|$)")
Webserver process writes PHP/PHAR file to web-accessible upload directory AIInstallation High
Catches the landing artifact of CVE-2026-48062 exploitation: php-fpm/w3wp/nginx/httpd/php-cgi creates a file ending in .php/.phar/.phtml/.phps inside writable, uploads, public, htdocs or wwwroot. The CodeIgniter advisory explicitly calls out `$file->move($path)` preserving the original client filename as the impact vector. Rationale: Article states impact requires applications that 'save uploaded files using the original client filename: $file->move($path), store uploads in a web-accessible directory'. The signature is unmistakable: webserver process creating PHP-extension file inside webroot/uploads. Cross-referenced with CodeIgniter4 docs on `$file->move()` and CWE-434. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html#moving-files • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1036.008 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Composer / Composer-installed Drush / wp-cli scaffold operations that write .php files via php.exe into vendor/public during development
  • Legitimate CMS plugin install/update flows where the webserver process writes new .php template files into /public/themes or /writable/cache
  • OPcache file_cache writing serialized .php files into /writable on first request
  • Sysadmin running composer install as the webserver user post-deploy
  • CodeIgniter writable/cache/* files that ship as .php (rare, but possible for compiled view caches)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer", "drush", "wp-cli", "artisan") or FolderPath has "writable\\cache")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: compute SHA256 of the dropped file, hexdump first 16 bytes to check for GIF/PNG magic preceding `<?php` (polyglot artifact), and check ImFileEvent / DeviceFileEvents for the originating HTTP POST window. Step 2 — Contain: quarantine the file, isolate the host, and apply web-root execute-deny ACLs to the upload directory (workaround listed in advisory). Step 3 — Hunt: search W3CIISLog/Nginx access logs for subsequent GETs to the file path, and pivot DeviceProcessEvents for webserver-spawned children (cmd/powershell/bash) within 60s of the write. Confirm CodeIgniter4 version and upgrade to >= 4.7.3.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php.exe", "w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2.exe", "caddy.exe")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phps" or FileName endswith ".inc"
| where FolderPath has_any ("uploads", "upload", "writable", "public", "htdocs", "wwwroot", "www", "avatar")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm", "php-cgi", "php.exe", "w3wp.exe", "httpd", "nginx", "apache2", "caddy")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php", "phar", "phtml", "phps", "inc")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("uploads", "upload", "writable", "public", "htdocs", "wwwroot", "www", "avatar")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP File Written by Webserver Process to Upload Directory (CVE-2026-48062)
id: 8e6f4f2a-3c1b-4d9a-b2e7-a1f5c8d4e012
description: Detects PHP/executable file written by webserver process into a web-accessible upload directory, consistent with CVE-2026-48062 CodeIgniter4 ext_in validation bypass exploitation
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
  - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1036.008
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\php-fpm.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\apache2.exe'
      - '\caddy.exe'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.phar'
      - '.phtml'
      - '.phps'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\uploads\'
      - '\upload\'
      - '\writable\'
      - '\public\'
      - '\htdocs\'
      - '\www\'
      - '\wwwroot\'
      - '\avatar\'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: high

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\php-fpm.exe OR *\\PHP-FPM.exe OR *\\php-cgi.exe OR *\\PHP-CGI.exe OR *\\php.exe OR *\\PHP.exe OR *\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.exe OR *\\nginx.exe OR *\\NGINX.exe OR *\\httpd.exe OR *\\caddy.exe) @TargetFilename:(*.php OR *.phar OR *.phtml OR *.phps) @TargetFilename:(*\\uploads\\* OR *\\upload\\* OR *\\writable\\* OR *\\public\\* OR *\\htdocs\\* OR *\\www\\* OR *\\wwwroot\\* OR *\\avatar\\*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|php|w3wp|httpd|nginx|apache2|caddy)\.exe$/i TargetFileName=/\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|inc)$/i
| regex("(?i)(uploads|writable|public|htdocs|wwwroot|www|avatar)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php.exe", "w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2.exe", "caddy.exe") by _time, Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where match(file_name, "(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|inc)$") | where match(file_path, "(?i)(uploads|upload|writable|public|htdocs|www|wwwroot|avatar)")
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php.exe", "w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2.exe", "caddy.exe") by _time, Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where match(file_name, "(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|inc)$") | where match(file_path, "(?i)(uploads|upload|writable|public|htdocs|www|wwwroot|avatar)")
HTTP GET to PHP/PHAR file inside CodeIgniter web-accessible upload directory AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for HTTP GET requests landing on PHP-executable files served from upload-style directories (writable/uploads/public/avatar). Per the advisory, RCE only materialises when 'PHP or other executable files run from that directory' — so an inbound GET to a recently-uploaded .php under /uploads is the moment of compromise. Rationale: Article states the conditions for RCE include 'store uploads in a web-accessible directory' and 'allow PHP or other executable files to run from that directory'. The GET to that exact path is the trigger event for code execution. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory workarounds (storing outside web root, disabling script execution). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html#moving-files
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate apps that intentionally serve dynamic PHP from /uploads (rare but exists in legacy CMS)
  • Web vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Burp, Acunetix) brute-forcing common webshell paths and getting 200s on real shells they didn't drop
  • Admin-area file-manager plugins that route requests through /uploads/index.php with rewrite rules
  • Static content CDN pre-warming requests against image URLs that share a path prefix
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus", "Acunetix", "Nuclei", "Burp", "sqlmap", "WPScan")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull csUserAgent, cIP, csReferer for the request; check whether the same path appears in any preceding file-write event by webserver process (correlate with the file-write UC). Step 2 — Contain: block source IP at WAF, take a forensic copy of the file, then delete it from disk and add an `.htaccess` / IIS handler-mapping rule denying script execution in the upload directory. Step 3 — Hunt: search the last 30 days of access logs for every GET to that file path and other .php files in the same directory; pivot DeviceProcessEvents for webserver-spawned children spawned in the seconds following each request.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in~ ("FileOpened", "FileCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php.exe", "w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2.exe", "caddy.exe")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phps"
| where FolderPath has_any ("uploads", "upload", "writable", "avatar", "public\\uploads")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), AccessCount=count() by DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where AccessCount >= 1
| order by LastSeen desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "GET"
| where scStatus == 200
| where csUriStem has_any ("/uploads/", "/upload/", "/avatar/", "/writable/", "/public/uploads/")
| where csUriStem endswith ".php" or csUriStem endswith ".phar" or csUriStem endswith ".phtml" or csUriStem endswith ".phps"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, csReferer, scStatus, TimeTaken
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HTTP GET to PHP File in CodeIgniter Upload Directory (CVE-2026-48062)

  selection_method:
    cs-method: 'GET'

#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|php|w3wp|httpd|nginx|apache2)\.exe$/i TargetFileName=/\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)$/i
| regex("(?i)(uploads|upload|writable|avatar|public\\\\uploads)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=GET Web.status=200 by _time, Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search url IN ("*/uploads/*.php", "*/uploads/*.phar", "*/uploads/*.phtml", "*/upload/*.php", "*/avatar/*.php", "*/writable/*.php", "*/public/avatar/*.php")
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=GET Web.status=200 by _time, Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search url IN ("*/uploads/*.php", "*/uploads/*.phar", "*/uploads/*.phtml", "*/upload/*.php", "*/avatar/*.php", "*/writable/*.php", "*/public/avatar/*.php")
Webserver process (php-fpm/w3wp/nginx) spawns OS shell or recon binary AIExploitation High
Detects post-exploitation execution from a CodeIgniter4 webshell dropped via CVE-2026-48062: php-fpm, php-cgi, php.exe, w3wp.exe, nginx.exe, httpd.exe or apache2.exe spawning cmd/powershell/pwsh/bash/sh or built-in recon LOLBins (whoami, net, wmic, systeminfo, nltest). This is the canonical webshell-to-shell pivot the OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet calls out. Rationale: Article states impact is 'arbitrary code execution' when uploads land in web-executable directories. The first observable RCE behaviour from a CodeIgniter4 webshell is the PHP runtime spawning a host shell or recon binary — a parent-child pair that almost never occurs in benign PHP web app operation. Cross-referenced with OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet and CWE-434. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy PHP apps using shell_exec() / exec() for image processing via ImageMagick (`convert.exe`) — but those rarely spawn cmd.exe/powershell.exe directly
  • Monitoring agents (Datadog Agent, New Relic) attached to the webserver process running periodic health probes via cmd /c
  • PHP scheduler libraries (Laravel queue worker on Windows) spawning cmd.exe to launch worker children
  • WordPress/Drupal cron via `wp-cron.php` shelling out to `php.exe` for batch jobs (rare on Windows)
  • DevOps deploy hooks that POST to a webhook endpoint and execute a shell script as part of CI/CD
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("datadog-agent", "newrelic", "appdynamics", "laravel\\artisan queue:work", "wp-cron.php") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("datadog-agent", "newrelic"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture full ProcessCommandLine for the child, walk the process tree backwards and forwards (children of cmd.exe, subsequent network connections from the webserver process), and pull the recent file-write events for that DeviceName to find the dropped webshell. Step 2 — Contain: kill the webserver process, isolate the host from network, snapshot disk + memory before reboot, and rotate any credentials the webserver had access to (DB creds, IAM keys, redis tokens). Step 3 — Hunt: scope to all CodeIgniter4 hosts in the estate, run the file-write UC across the last 30 days, and pivot on the attacker source IP and User-Agent through WAF/access logs. Confirm CodeIgniter4 version everywhere and upgrade to >= 4.7.3.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php.exe", "w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2.exe", "caddy.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "bash.exe", "sh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "wget.exe", "curl.exe", "wmic.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "nltest.exe", "hostname.exe", "arp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentName = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentName in ("php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php.exe", "w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2.exe", "caddy.exe")
| where ChildName in ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "bash.exe", "sh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "wget.exe", "curl.exe", "wmic.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "nltest.exe", "hostname.exe", "arp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48062")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48062")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,

A new malware loader called GoFlateLoader has been quietly spreading across the internet, and what makes it stand out is not how complex it is but how effective a simple trick has made it. Written in the Go programming language, this loader has one job: to decode and drop dangerous information-stealing programs onto a victim&#8217;s [&#8230;] The post GoFlateLoader Uses Massive PE Overlay to Deliver Lumma, Vidar, and StealC Infostealers appeared first on Cyber Security News .

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

"841c9297cb8a2e0ff89433d13c05bfc760eb2e98e251cb8fa785d2ad7cbac05f", "ece7c48eb411b24f26762ede83badb4a644c41d5777129381ac2541804d64fc2", "421ce2d2f49c23bbe9f60ef3b9cd38d7eb912ce02e56a61837656210069bd9e2", "121c2dc793b3873f75a29ec02241f94136de19c049382a50a50d0d5b99507073", "2415db5081cec9bfd14ad6da1a66169fd96f13a49010c319a73d1ed6fafd4efa", "d9917ade3b4c125a95b5d3e6343cde26145dfbf569bd7e2a843fd0c6fc8ddc28", "4cf6893756f441522b94b36f10e5de0e47aeed4743f95c51650746d1ecf97e3d", "8b89d6c9152d3aab97aadd515ecb69ca72654db2f25425759ba4b646853d737d", "90ce4ff9da23ac150da0a8e17930cab1e369aa349fdc1b65691b70369145664a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b88c5744975d2abb447aecc6c090fee9f8580413f4612eecdc6ed1973e8a1739", "ed5ae7f36453c5a23e9868a5729d67e0549a11f6dea54f5f52d654a8f51d4902", "841c9297cb8a2e0ff89433d13c05bfc760eb2e98e251cb8fa785d2ad7cbac05f", "ece7c48eb411b24f26762ede83badb4a644c41d5777129381ac2541804d64fc2", "421ce2d2f49c23bbe9f60ef3b9cd38d7eb912ce02e56a61837656210069bd9e2", "121c2dc793b3873f75a29ec02241f94136de19c049382a50a50d0d5b99507073", "2415db5081cec9bfd14ad6da1a66169fd96f13a49010c319a73d1ed6fafd4efa", "d9917ade3b4c125a95b5d3e6343cde26145dfbf569bd7e2a843fd0c6fc8ddc28", "4cf6893756f441522b94b36f10e5de0e47aeed4743f95c51650746d1ecf97e3d", "8b89d6c9152d3aab97aadd515ecb69ca72654db2f25425759ba4b646853d737d", "90ce4ff9da23ac150da0a8e17930cab1e369aa349fdc1b65691b70369145664a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
