Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:

            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:

level: high

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Editor/AI-tool auto-execute config dropped in developer project (Miasma/Hades) AIInstallation High
Hunts the specific filenames Miasma and Hades drop into repos so the payload fires on folder-open or AI-session start: .vscode/tasks.json, .vscode/setup.mjs, .claude/setup.mjs, .claude/settings.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .gemini/settings.json, .github/setup.js. These never appear in package manifests or lockfile diffs, so SCA tools miss them — file-system telemetry is the only way to catch them. Rationale: Article Table 1 enumerates the exact filenames Miasma/Hades drop and the trigger each one fires under (folderOpen, SessionStart, settings injection). These paths never appear in package.json/requirements.txt and never legitimately materialise in fresh checkouts unless explicitly committed — high-fidelity for the worm.
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1554 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate VS Code workspace using runOn:folderOpen for a project bootstrap script
  • Developer manually adding a .claude/setup.mjs as part of an internal AI-tooling repo
  • Internal scaffolder/cookiecutter writing .vscode/tasks.json into new projects
  • Onboarding scripts that drop .github/setup.js into engineering repos
  • Git clone of a curated internal template that ships these files by design
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cookiecutter","yo ","create-react-app","create-next-app","degit")) and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","code-insiders.exe") and FolderPath has @"\.vscode\")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: open the file and check whether tasks.json declares runOn:folderOpen, whether setup.mjs/setup.js executes a network fetch (Bun runtime, base64 blob), and whether the file landed via `git pull` or an npm/pip install (check InitiatingProcessFileName). Step 2 — Contain: pause the developer's git pushes and rotate npm/PyPI publishing tokens for that user via the registry UI (per article: tokens are the worm's spreader). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on this DeviceId to UC2 (binding.gyp), UC3 (Bun download), UC4 (__init__.py hook), UC5 (.npmrc read), and UC6 (npm publish/twine upload) within the last 48h.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.vscode\" and FileName in~ ("tasks.json","setup.mjs"))
    or (FolderPath has @"\.claude\" and FileName in~ ("setup.mjs","settings.json"))
    or (FolderPath has @"\.cursor\rules\" and FileName =~ "setup.mdc")
    or (FolderPath has @"\.gemini\" and FileName =~ "settings.json")
    or (FolderPath has @"\.github\" and FileName =~ "setup.js")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated" or EventType == "FileModified"
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\" and TargetFileName in~ ("tasks.json","setup.mjs"))
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\" and TargetFileName in~ ("setup.mjs","settings.json"))
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\.cursor\rules\" and TargetFileName =~ "setup.mdc")
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\.gemini\" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json")
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\.github\" and TargetFileName =~ "setup.js")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256

Miasma Phantom Gyp: tiny binding.gyp triggers native build code execution AIExploitation High
Hunts the Phantom Gyp technique: Miasma ships a ~157-byte binding.gyp inside an npm package that runs arbitrary code through the native build step during npm install, sidestepping preinstall/postinstall script checks. Pivots on small binding.gyp writes followed by node-gyp / cl.exe / clang / gcc spawning from npm-cache directories. Rationale: Article explicitly names the 157-byte binding.gyp as Miasma's 'Phantom Gyp' execution vector, and explains it triggers on native-build step bypassing preinstall/postinstall hooks. The size band (50-400 bytes) catches the tiny payload-launcher gyp while leaving legitimate ones (kilobytes) alone, and the parent-process chain (npm→node-gyp→compiler) pinpoints when it actually fires.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1204.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A genuinely minimal native module (rare but legal — e.g. a stub binding.gyp during scaffolding)
  • Developer experimenting with node-gyp via `node-gyp configure` on a learning project
  • CI agents installing native deps (better-sqlite3, sharp, fsevents) with small binding.gyp files
  • node-pre-gyp prebuilt-binary flows that still touch binding.gyp briefly
  • npm rebuild during postinstall hooks of legitimately published native packages
Suppression filter
| where not (BindingGypPath has_any ("node_modules\\better-sqlite3","node_modules\\sharp","node_modules\\fsevents","node_modules\\node-sass","node_modules\\bcrypt"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: cat the binding.gyp identified and look for inline `actions` blocks invoking python, curl, or base64 — the article says Miasma uses the native-build action as the execution sink. Step 2 — Contain: kill the npm/node process tree on the host, freeze the developer's npm publish token, and quarantine the package directory under node_modules/. Step 3 — Hunt: from the developer's npm account, list all packages they can publish (`npm access list packages`) and review the last 24h of publish events for unexpected versions — the worm republishes every reachable package.
let SmallBindingGyp = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileSize between (50 .. 400)
| project FileTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, BindingGypPath=FolderPath, BindingGypSize=FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","node-gyp.exe","npm.cmd","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cl.exe","clang.exe","clang++.exe","gcc.exe","link.exe","python.exe","node-gyp.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("binding.gyp","node-gyp rebuild","node-gyp configure")
| join kind=inner SmallBindingGyp on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (FileTime .. FileTime + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, BindingGypPath, BindingGypSize, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let SmallBindingGyp = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where TargetFileSize between (50 .. 400)
| project FileTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, BindingGypPath=TargetFilePath, BindingGypSize=TargetFileSize;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","node-gyp.exe","npm.cmd","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cl.exe","clang.exe","clang++.exe","gcc.exe","link.exe","python.exe","node-gyp.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("binding.gyp","node-gyp rebuild","node-gyp configure")
| join kind=inner SmallBindingGyp on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (FileTime .. FileTime + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, BindingGypPath, BindingGypSize, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessCommandLine
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\node-gyp.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NPM.exe)) (@Image:(*\\cl.exe OR *\\clang.exe OR *\\gcc.exe OR *\\python.exe OR *\\link.exe OR *\\node-gyp.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*binding.gyp* OR *"node-gyp rebuild"*))

| ImageFileName=/(cl|clang|clang\+\+|gcc|link|python|node-gyp)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/binding\.gyp|node-gyp\s+(rebuild|configure)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Hades on-import: Bun runtime downloaded by Python or Node AIDelivery High
Hades' PyPI variant fires from an obfuscated one-liner in __init__.py that downloads a standalone Bun runtime and runs a JavaScript payload through it. Hunts python.exe or node.exe pulling bun.sh / oven-sh/bun GitHub assets, then spawning bun.exe with a JS file argument. Rationale: Article: 'the hook downloads a standalone Bun runtime and runs a JavaScript payload' on import. Python or Node spawning a downloader for the Bun release asset is a unique behavioural signature for Hades — legitimate Python/Node code essentially never pulls Bun.
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.007 T1027.009
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer manually evaluating Bun for a project and curling the release zip
  • Internal tutorial or hackathon scaffolding that wraps Bun installation in Python
  • CI image-build script that uses python to fetch language toolchains including Bun
  • Cross-runtime benchmarking script that legitimately downloads multiple runtimes
  • Developer using a `bun` install wrapper from their `pip` toolchain
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("benchmark","runtime-eval","hackathon","cookiecutter") and AccountName has "ci-runner")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the parent Python/Node process; check the command line for an `__init__.py` path or an obfuscated one-liner (exec/eval/base64). Confirm whether bun.exe was actually written and executed (DeviceFileEvents + DeviceProcessEvents). Step 2 — Contain: kill bun.exe + the parent interpreter, isolate the host, and rotate any PyPI/npm tokens stored under that user. Step 3 — Hunt: review pip and import activity on the host for the package whose __init__.py is the loader; pivot to UC4 to find the obfuscated hook write and to UC5 for credential-file reads.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","py.exe","pythonw.exe","node.exe")
| where (FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
         and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh","oven-sh/bun","bun-windows-x64","bun-linux-x64","bun-darwin"))
    or (FileName =~ "bun.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
| union (
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","py.exe","pythonw.exe","node.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("bun.sh","oven-sh/bun","bun-windows","bun-linux","bun-darwin")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
)
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","py.exe","pythonw.exe","node.exe")
| where (TargetProcessName has_any ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
         and TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh","oven-sh/bun","bun-windows-x64","bun-linux-x64","bun-darwin"))
    or TargetProcessName =~ "bun.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| union (
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has_any ("bun.sh","oven-sh/bun","bun-windows","bun-linux","bun-darwin")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod
)

Obfuscated one-line hook injected into __init__.py (Hades persistence) AIInstallation Medium
Hades' loader is an obfuscated one-line hook embedded in a package's __init__.py that fires on import. Hunts file writes to __init__.py containing exec/eval/base64 one-liners, lambdas with __import__, or compile() inline — the shapes the article describes for the Hades branch. Rationale: Article: 'The malicious code is an obfuscated one-line hook embedded in a package's __init__.py' that runs on import. The filename + obfuscation tokens (exec/eval/base64/__import__/compile) are direct lifts from the Hades description. Filtering out legit pip/poetry/conda writes leaves the signal.
ATT&CKT1027 T1059.006 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • pyinstaller-style package builders that legitimately write __init__.py with exec()
  • Developer editing a package's __init__.py manually in an IDE that hits the file_event channel
  • conda/mamba writing __init__.py during environment creation (filter shouldn't catch but edge cases exist)
  • setuptools entry-point scripts emitted by package builds
  • Lazy-loading patterns in legitimate frameworks (e.g. django, sqlalchemy) that use __import__ in __init__.py
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "python.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.py develop","setup.py install","pip install -e"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: open the modified __init__.py and grep for exec(/eval(/base64.b64decode/__import__/compile — if any are present in a one-liner format the package is suspect. Cross-check the package name against PyPI Hades IOC bundles (ensmallen and related ML/bioinformatics packages per the article). Step 2 — Contain: pip uninstall the package, isolate the host, and rotate any PyPI tokens cached on the device. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC3 (Bun download) and UC5 (.pypirc read) on the same host; check recent `import` activity in active Python processes (DeviceImageLoadEvents for the package's .pyd modules).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

npm/PyPI publishing credentials read by package-manager or shell process AIActions on Objectives Medium
Miasma and Hades search for npm and PyPI publishing tokens on the developer machine and use them to republish infected versions of every package the token can publish — the worm propagation mechanism. Hunts reads of .npmrc, ~/.pypirc, npm-token files, and Windows Credential Manager npm/pypi entries by shells, interpreters, or downloaded runtimes. Rationale: Article: 'it searches for npm and PyPI publishing tokens, then republishes infected versions of every package that token can publish. Each new victim becomes a new spreader.' .npmrc and .pypirc are the canonical credential files; the FP cut is excluding the legitimate package-manager processes that have a real reason to read them.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using a personal script in PowerShell to inspect their own .npmrc
  • CI agent reading .npmrc through cat/Get-Content in a build step
  • Backup or sync utility (OneDrive, Dropbox) touching the file
  • IDE indexers (VS Code, JetBrains) opening .npmrc as part of project scan
  • Cursor/Claude Code reading .npmrc as part of AI assistant context (could be benign)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","code-insiders.exe","cursor.exe","idea64.exe","pycharm64.exe","webstorm64.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--type=renderer","--no-sandbox"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the reading process tree — is the parent an IDE (likely FP) or a bun/node/python chain originating from UC3/UC4 (high TP)? Step 2 — Contain: immediately revoke the token via `npm token revoke` / PyPI account settings and rotate; quarantine the host. Step 3 — Hunt: list every package the token had publish rights to (`npm access list packages <user>` / PyPI ownership page) and pull the last 72h of publish events for unexpected new versions — the worm publishes within minutes of token theft per article.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ (".npmrc",".pypirc","npm-token") or FolderPath has @"\npm\_authToken"
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileOpened","FileModified","FileCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","node.exe","python.exe","bun.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","py.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("npm.exe","pip.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","twine.exe","poetry.exe","uv.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath endswith ".npmrc" or TargetFilePath endswith ".pypirc" or TargetFilePath has "npm-token" or TargetFilePath has @"\npm\_authToken"
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","pip.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","twine.exe","poetry.exe","uv.exe"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","node.exe","python.exe","bun.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","py.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath
title: Miasma/Hades worm — npm/PyPI publishing credentials read by shell or runtime
id: 6f1c2a90-2b54-4f8a-9c1e-b2e4d8a51005
description: Detects reads of .npmrc, .pypirc, or npm _authToken files by powershell/cmd/node/python/bun/wscript/cscript — the credential-harvest step the worm uses to republish infected packages.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-and-hades-are-spreading-now-detect-them-on-developer-machines-with-suspicious-files
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1555
  - attack.t1005
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: windows
detection:
  files:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\.npmrc'
      - '\.pypirc'
      - '\npm-token'
    TargetFilename|contains: '\npm\_authToken'
  bad_readers:

      - '\powershell.exe'

      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\twine.exe'
      - '\poetry.exe'
      - '\uv.exe'
  condition: files and bad_readers and not good_readers
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\.npmrc OR *\\.pypirc OR *\\npm-token OR *\\npm\\_authToken*)) (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\python.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\Bun.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\py.exe)) -@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\pip.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\twine.exe OR *\\poetry.exe OR *\\uv.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo
| TargetFileName=/(\\\.npmrc|\\\.pypirc|\\npm-token|\\npm\\_authToken)$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|node|python|bun|wscript|cscript|py)\.exe$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(npm|pip|yarn|pnpm|twine|poetry|uv)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name=".npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_name=".pypirc" OR Filesystem.file_name="npm-token" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\npm\\_authToken*") (Filesystem.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="pwsh.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="cmd.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="node.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="python.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="bun.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="wscript.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="cscript.exe") NOT (Filesystem.process_name="npm.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="pip.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="yarn.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="pnpm.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="twine.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="poetry.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Worm propagation: npm publish or twine upload from non-interactive parent AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the worm's self-replication step: npm publish, yarn publish, pnpm publish, or twine upload invoked from a non-interactive parent (node interpreter inside a payload, bun.exe, python.exe running an obfuscated hook). Catches the moment the compromised developer's token is used to republish infected packages back to the registry. Rationale: Article: '113 repositories across dozens of accounts… spread across 73 repositories in under two minutes' via automated republishing. The high-signal pivot is npm/twine publish whose parent is a runtime interpreter rather than an interactive shell — humans publish from terminals, worms publish from inside their payload.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1567 T1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI release scripts that wrap `npm publish` in a node-based release tool (e.g. semantic-release, np)
  • Custom Python release tooling invoking twine upload as a subprocess
  • Lerna/Nx monorepo tooling that wraps publish from inside node
  • Developer-authored release wrapper scripts run from PowerShell
  • Internal package promotion scripts called from python build orchestrators
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("semantic-release","\\np\\","lerna publish","nx release","@changesets/cli"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture the full parent chain — was it semantic-release / np / lerna (likely legit) or an unfamiliar node/python script running from a package directory (likely the worm)? List the packages and versions published in the last 60 minutes. Step 2 — Contain: revoke the npm/PyPI publish token immediately and unpublish/yank the suspicious versions via the registry (`npm unpublish <pkg>@<ver>` within 72h, PyPI `yank`); isolate host. Step 3 — Hunt: across the org, query for every host whose user owns publish rights to the affected packages and look for UC1/UC3/UC4 hits in the last 7 days; coordinate with npm/PyPI security teams (per article StepSecurity escalates these).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "publish")
    or (FileName =~ "twine.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "upload")
    or (FileName in~ ("python.exe","py.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("twine","upload"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","python.exe","bun.exe","py.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","code.exe","code-insiders.exe","cursor.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","conhost.exe","cmd.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","exec(","eval(","base64","-EncodedCommand")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (TargetProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","npm.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "publish")
    or (TargetProcessName =~ "twine.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "upload")
    or (TargetProcessName has_any ("python.exe","py.exe") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "twine" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "upload")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","python.exe","bun.exe","py.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where not (ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("explorer.exe","code.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","conhost.exe"))
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("exec(","eval(","base64","-EncodedCommand")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
title: Miasma/Hades worm propagation — npm publish or twine upload from non-interactive parent
id: 6f1c2a90-2b54-4f8a-9c1e-b2e4d8a51006
description: Detects npm/yarn/pnpm publish or twine upload spawned by a runtime (node/python/bun) rather than an interactive shell or IDE — the article's described worm-spread step where stolen tokens republish infected packages.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-and-hades-are-spreading-now-detect-them-on-developer-machines-with-suspicious-files
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.t1496
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  npm_publish:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'publish'
  twine_upload:
    Image|endswith: '\twine.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'upload'
  bad_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '\py.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  condition: (npm_publish or twine_upload) and bad_parent
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe) AND @CommandLine:*publish*) OR (@Image:(*\\twine.exe OR *\\Twine.exe) AND @CommandLine:*upload*)) @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\python.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\Bun.exe OR *\\py.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/(npm\.exe|npm\.cmd|yarn\.exe|pnpm\.exe)$/i CommandLine=/publish/i) OR (ImageFileName=/twine\.exe$/i CommandLine=/upload/i)
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|python|bun|py|wscript|cscript|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="npm.exe" OR Processes.process_name="npm.cmd" OR Processes.process_name="yarn.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pnpm.exe" OR Processes.process_name="twine.exe") (Processes.process="*publish*" OR Processes.process="*upload*") (Processes.parent_process_name="node.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="python.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="py.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="wscript.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="cscript.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="powershell.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="npm.exe" OR Processes.process_name="npm.cmd" OR Processes.process_name="yarn.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pnpm.exe" OR Processes.process_name="twine.exe") (Processes.process="*publish*" OR Processes.process="*upload*") (Processes.parent_process_name="node.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="python.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="py.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="wscript.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="cscript.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="powershell.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"

          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution

status: experimental

    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"

| order by files desc

| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores

    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e") or SHA1 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e") or MD5 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e") or SHA1 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e") or MD5 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains

Bun runtime spawned by npm/node install context (Shai-Hulud / Mini Shai-Hulud) AIInstallation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud worm pattern where a postinstall or preinstall hook downloads and executes the Bun runtime during npm install. Bun appearing as a child of npm.exe or node.exe outside a developer's documented toolchain is high-signal because both worm families used Bun as a portable execution layer before launching credential stealers. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit quotes: Shai-Hulud 'installed the Bun runtime during setup, ran TruffleHog' and Mini Shai-Hulud 'planting a preinstall hook that pulled the Bun runtime'. Bun-as-child-of-npm-or-node is the worm's signature execution-layer pivot.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running 'npm install -g bun' as part of intentional toolchain setup
  • CI/CD pipeline installing Bun via npm as a build dependency for a Bun-based project
  • Polyglot monorepo with both Node and Bun where bun is invoked as bunx via npm scripts
  • Migration tooling that installs Bun alongside Node for compatibility testing
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install -g bun","install --global bun") and AccountName in~ ("<known-dev-accounts>")) and not (DeviceName startswith "BUILD-" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "package.json" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "bun")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the parent npm command line and the package being installed (look at the npm cache or node_modules path near the event). Identify the originating package.json and whether the user actually ran 'npm install' for a new dependency vs an intentional Bun install. Step 2 — Contain: if Bun launched from a node_modules postinstall context, isolate the host, kill the Bun process tree, and snapshot ~/.bun and node_modules/.package-lock.json for IR. Step 3 — Hunt: across the fleet, search for the same package@version installed in the last 14 days; check DeviceFileEvents for trufflehog / git push to non-corporate github.com remotes; rotate any tokens (npm, GitHub, AWS) that lived on the host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node","npm-cli.js") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe")
| where FileName =~ "bun.exe" or FileName =~ "bun"
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh/install","irm bun.sh","curl -fsSL https://bun.sh","powershell -c \"irm bun.sh")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FileName,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node")
| where ActingProcessName has "bun"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh/install","irm bun.sh","curl -fsSL https://bun.sh")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun Runtime Spawned by npm or node Install Context
id: 9c2f6f3e-1d8a-4f63-a5b4-4d7d6d2c1aa1
description: Detects Bun runtime being launched or downloaded as a child of npm/node, the Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud worm pattern
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent_image:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  child_bun_binary:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bun.exe'
  child_bun_cmdline:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'bun.sh/install'
      - 'irm bun.sh'
      - 'curl -fsSL https://bun.sh'
  condition: parent_image and (child_bun_binary or child_bun_cmdline)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\NPM.EXE OR *\NODE.EXE) (@Image:(*\bun.exe OR *\Bun.exe OR *\BUN.EXE) OR @CommandLine:(*"bun.sh/install"* OR *"irm bun.sh"* OR *"curl -fsSL https://bun.sh"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/(\\|\/)bun(\.exe)?$/i OR CommandLine=/(bun\.sh\/install|irm\s+bun\.sh|curl\s+-fsSL\s+https:\/\/bun\.sh)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm-cli.js","node","npm")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bun.exe","bun") OR Processes.process="*bun.sh/install*" OR Processes.process="*irm*bun.sh*" OR Processes.process="*curl*bun.sh*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

TruffleHog credential scanner spawned from npm install (Shai-Hulud signature) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects TruffleHog being executed as a child of npm.exe / node.exe — the Shai-Hulud worm specifically invoked TruffleHog from its postinstall hook to scrape secrets out of the developer environment before exfiltrating them to public GitHub repos. TruffleHog is a legitimate tool, but its execution under an install lifecycle is anomalous outside of explicit secret-scanning CI workflows. Rationale: Direct quote from article: Shai-Hulud 'installed the Bun runtime during setup, ran TruffleHog to scrape secrets, and dumped them into public GitHub repos.' TruffleHog as a child of npm/node is the credential-access leg of the worm and almost never legitimate outside a deliberate secret-scanning workflow.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1195.002 T1552.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal CI job that installs trufflehog via npm wrapper as a pre-commit secrets-scan step
  • Security team running TruffleHog locally after 'npm i -g @trufflesecurity/trufflehog'
  • Test/lab environment validating TruffleHog detection rules
  • Developer evaluating npm-published trufflehog wrappers in a sandbox
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pre-commit","secret-scan","--ci") and DeviceName startswith "CI-") and not (AccountName in~ ("<security-team-svc-accounts>"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture InitiatingProcessCommandLine to see which npm script triggered TruffleHog and which package owns that script (read package.json from InitiatingProcessFolderPath). Pull the trufflehog command line — flags like '--git', '--filesystem', '--regex' indicate aggressive secret scraping. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host, rotate all developer secrets (npm tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS keys, SSH keys, crypto wallets) immediately, and quarantine node_modules. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the offending package@version across the org; check for outbound git pushes to non-corp github.com remotes (Shai-Hulud's exfil pattern), and audit recent commits to public GitHub repos owned by the user/org for credential dumps.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node","npm-cli.js")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe")
| where FileName has "trufflehog"
   or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FileName,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node")
| where ActingProcessName has "trufflehog" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
