Nx s1ngularity telemetry.js postinstall script execution AIInstallation High
Detects execution of telemetry.js by Node under an npm install lifecycle — the named payload from the August 2025 Nx s1ngularity compromise where a stolen publish token pushed malicious Nx versions whose postinstall script (telemetry.js) scraped GitHub tokens, npm credentials, SSH keys, and crypto wallets, then uploaded them to public GitHub repos. Rationale: Anchored on article's named payload: 'Nx s1ngularity, August 2025. A stolen publish token pushed malicious Nx versions whose postinstall script, telemetry.js, ran on install.' telemetry.js + node_modules + nx path components is a tight three-way conjunction unlikely to collide with legitimate telemetry scripts.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Nx versions that historically shipped a real telemetry.js (pre-compromise) on first install
  • Internal monorepo using a project named 'nx' with its own analytics script called telemetry.js
  • Other npm packages that ship a generically-named telemetry.js (low likelihood given the node_modules constraint)
  • Developer running 'node ./node_modules/nx/telemetry.js' directly for diagnostics
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--diag" and AccountName in~ ("<known-dev-accounts>"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read the SHA256 of node_modules/nx/telemetry.js on disk and compare against the legit Nx-distributed file; pull the version string from node_modules/nx/package.json — Nx s1ngularity hit specific versions, confirm which one is on disk. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host, force-remove the affected node_modules, rotate GitHub tokens, npm tokens, SSH keys and crypto wallet keys for the developer account. Step 3 — Hunt: pull DeviceFileEvents for any FileCreated to public GitHub remotes or to ~/.config/<exfil-dir>, search for git push to repos the user doesn't own (the Nx worm dumped 2,300 credentials to attacker repos), and review npm install command lines across the fleet for the malicious nx@version.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node","npm-cli.js")
   or FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "telemetry.js"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("node_modules","\\nx\\","/nx/")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FileName,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node")
   or ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "telemetry.js"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node_modules","\\nx\\","/nx/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Implicit node-gyp rebuild from binding.gyp during npm install AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the article's specific 'spotless package.json' execution path: a dependency ships a binding.gyp and npm runs an implicit node-gyp rebuild during install, executing code even when no preinstall/install/postinstall script is declared. Pivots on node-gyp spawning compilers (python, MSBuild, link.exe, cl.exe) from a node_modules subtree. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit warning: 'When a package ships a binding.gyp, npm runs an implicit node-gyp rebuild for it during install, so a dependency with a spotless package.json can still execute code just by carrying that one build file.' This is a hunting pivot (high FP on native packages like sqlite3, bcrypt, sharp, canvas) — analyst reviews emerging unique package names.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006 T1127
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native-binding packages: sqlite3, bcrypt, sharp, canvas, node-sass, better-sqlite3, node-pty — all run node-gyp rebuild on install
  • Electron apps installing native modules during 'npm rebuild'
  • CI build images warming up node_modules with native dependencies
  • Developer machines on first 'npm install' of a Node.js backend project with native deps
  • Postgres / Oracle / MS-SQL native client packages compiling on install
Suppression filter
and not (Packages has_any ("sqlite3","bcrypt","sharp","canvas","node-sass","better-sqlite3","node-pty","node-sass","grpc","node-expat"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: list distinct package names under node_modules whose binding.gyp triggered the rebuild — compare against your org's allowlist of known native-binding deps (sqlite3, bcrypt, sharp, etc.). Anything unfamiliar gets a deep look. Step 2 — Contain: for unknown packages, freeze the build, fetch the tarball from the npm cache and unpack binding.gyp + the .gyp targets; look for suspicious actions in the gyp 'actions' clause (curl, bash, file writes outside the project). Step 3 — Hunt: across the fleet, pivot on the unknown package@version; check DeviceNetworkEvents for the build host reaching unexpected hosts during the rebuild window; consider adopting npm 11.16.0+ today so node-gyp rebuilds without an allowlist entry warn instead of run.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","node-gyp.exe")
        or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp rebuild","node-gyp configure","binding.gyp"))
| where FileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","msbuild.exe","cl.exe","link.exe","cmake.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has "binding.gyp"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules"
   or ProcessCommandLine has "node_modules"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize Count = count(),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            Packages = make_set(extract(@"node_modules[\\/]([^\\/]+)", 1, InitiatingProcessCommandLine), 10)
        by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","node.exe","node-gyp.exe")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp rebuild","node-gyp configure","binding.gyp")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","msbuild.exe","cl.exe","link.exe","cmake.exe")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "binding.gyp"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "node_modules" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules"
| summarize Count = count(),
            SampleCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated)
        by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ParentProcessName
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\node-gyp.exe OR *\NPM.EXE OR *\NODE.EXE) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*"node-gyp rebuild"* OR *"binding.gyp"*)) (@Image:(*\python.exe OR *\python3.exe OR *\msbuild.exe OR *\MSBuild.exe OR *\cl.exe OR *\link.exe OR *\cmake.exe) OR @CommandLine:*binding.gyp*) @CommandLine:*node_modules*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|node-gyp)(\.exe)?$/i OR regex("node-gyp\s+rebuild|binding\.gyp", field=ParentCommandLine))
| ImageFileName=/(python3?|msbuild|cl|link|cmake)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/binding\.gyp/i
| regex("node_modules", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
| _count > 0
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count values(Processes.process) as cmdlines min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node","node-gyp.exe") OR Processes.parent_process="*node-gyp*rebuild*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("python.exe","python3.exe","msbuild.exe","cl.exe","link.exe","cmake.exe") OR Processes.process="*binding.gyp*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmdlines min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node","node-gyp.exe") OR Processes.parent_process="*node-gyp*rebuild*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("python.exe","python3.exe","msbuild.exe","cl.exe","link.exe","cmake.exe") OR Processes.process="*binding.gyp*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Git publish-to-public-GitHub from npm install context (Shai-Hulud exfil) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Shai-Hulud and Nx s1ngularity exfiltration pattern: a postinstall script invokes git to create a public repo or push harvested secrets to attacker-controlled GitHub repositories. The article calls out both worms dumping credentials into public GitHub repos — git.exe spawned as a descendant of npm/node with push/create-repo operations is a high-fidelity exfil signal. Rationale: Anchored on article's repeated exfil pattern: Nx s1ngularity 'uploaded them to public GitHub repos' and Shai-Hulud 'dumped them into public GitHub repos.' Time-correlated join (git push or gh repo create within 5min of npm install on the same host) is the worm's hand-off from credential collection to exfil. webhook.site (pre-extracted IOC) is a related but distinct exfil channel covered by generic egress hunting; the GitHub-public-repo path is what these specific worms used.
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1195.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • semantic-release or release-it lifecycle scripts that git-tag and push as part of legitimate publish flow
  • Documentation generators (typedoc, docusaurus) that commit and push generated docs to a gh-pages branch via npm scripts
  • Monorepo tooling (Lerna, Nx, Turborepo) that runs git operations during 'npm install' lifecycle
  • CI runners performing legitimate gh CLI operations alongside npm install
  • Husky / lint-staged invoking git from npm install lifecycle
Suppression filter
and not (NpmCmd has_any ("semantic-release","release-it","husky","lint-staged","lerna","docusaurus") and GitCmd has_any ("gh-pages","refs/tags/"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture the git remote URL the push targeted — corporate github.example.com is benign, push to github.com under an unknown org/user is the red flag. Pull the npm install command line to see which package triggered the chain. Step 2 — Contain: revoke the developer's GitHub PAT and SSH keys, force-pull the public repo URL and snapshot its contents for IR (the worms dumped credential bundles there), isolate the host. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the package@version in the npm install command across the fleet; check the GitHub audit log for newly-created public repos by org users in the last 7 days; rotate any npm/AWS/SSH credentials that lived on the host; look at DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to api.github.com from node.exe across other dev workstations.
let WindowMin = 5m;
let NpmInstall = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node","npm-cli.js")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","ci","rebuild")
    | project InstallStart = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName,
              NpmCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","git","gh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("push","gh repo create","api.github.com/user/repos","--public","git remote add")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner NpmInstall on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (InstallStart .. InstallStart + WindowMin)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          NpmCmd, GitImage = FileName, GitCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 5m;
let NpmInstall = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","ci","rebuild")
    | project InstallStart = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NpmCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("git.exe","git","gh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("push","gh repo create","api.github.com/user/repos","--public","git remote add")
| join kind=inner NpmInstall on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (InstallStart .. InstallStart + WindowMin)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          NpmCmd, GitImage = ActingProcessName, GitCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\NPM.EXE OR *\NODE.EXE) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*"npm install"* OR *"npm ci"* OR *"npm rebuild"*)) (@Image:(*\git.exe OR *\Git.exe OR *\gh.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*push* OR *"gh repo create"* OR *"api.github.com/user/repos"* OR *--public* OR *"git remote add"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|sh|bash|cmd|powershell)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/(git|gh|curl|wget)(\.exe)?$/i
| CommandLine=/(push|gh\s+repo\s+create|api\.github\.com\/user\/repos|--public|git\s+remote\s+add)/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(npm|node)(\.exe)?$/i CommandLine=/install|ci|rebuild/i | rename(field=CommandLine, as=NpmCmd) | rename(field=_time, as=NpmTime)}, field=aid)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, NpmCmd], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node","sh.exe","bash.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")) AND Processes.process_name IN ("git.exe","git","gh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") AND (Processes.process="*push*" OR Processes.process="*repos*" OR Processes.process="*api.github.com*" OR Processes.process="*--public*" OR Processes.process="*gh repo create*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm","node","sh.exe","bash.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")) AND Processes.process_name IN ("git.exe","git","gh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") AND (Processes.process="*push*" OR Processes.process="*repos*" OR Processes.process="*api.github.com*" OR Processes.process="*--public*" OR Processes.process="*gh repo create*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |

references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase

tags:

detection:
    selection_path:

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'

    filter_browser:

            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /mcp on TCP 8080 (CVE-2026-48039) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for inbound HTTP POST requests to the /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080 from public source IPs, signalling exploitation of the AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch() bypass in pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp ≤ 1.0.101 where unauthenticated requests reach downstream MCP tool handlers without a 401 response. Rationale: Targets the exact transport described in the advisory: POST /mcp on the default port 8080 from an unauthenticated, network-reachable caller. The article's PoC explicitly shows 'POST /mcp HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:8080' returning 200 OK without auth headers - external + POST + /mcp + 8080 is the clean signature of exploitation when the server is internet-exposed. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48039
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal monitoring or health-check probes hitting /mcp on 8080 from corporate subnets
  • Authorised penetration tests of the MCP service
  • Developer load-testing the MCP endpoint from a VPN-attached jumphost
  • Legitimate MCP client integrations from partner SaaS IPs
  • Vulnerability scanner sweeps (Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7) from known ranges
Suppression filter
| where not (SourceIP in ("<known-scanner-ip>","<pentest-ip>")) and not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Rapid7","healthcheck"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the source IP, confirm it is genuinely external (not a NAT'd internal scanner or pentest range). Check User-Agent and headers; legitimate MCP clients carry a Streamable HTTP Accept header. Inspect the JSON-RPC body for a 'tools/call' method and capture which tool was invoked. Step 2 — Contain: if external, immediately firewall-block the source IP, take the MCP server off the internet (move behind an authenticated reverse proxy), and rotate META_ACCESS_TOKEN at the Meta Business Manager. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC2 (Graph API access_token leakage) for the same host and 24h window; review meta-ads-mcp application logs for tool invocations that returned Graph API errors (these are the responses that exfiltrate the token); check Meta Ads Manager activity log for unexpected ad-account reads/writes.

title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to MCP Endpoint on Port 8080
id: c4b9e2a1-d5f8-4c3e-9a7b-1d6f4e8a2c5b
description: Detects HTTP POST to /mcp on TCP 8080 - matches the CVE-2026-48039 exploitation pattern against pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp ≤ 1.0.101
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - cve.2026.48039
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: 'POST'
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/mcp'
    s-port: 8080
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Internal smoke tests of the MCP server
  - Authorised pen-test sweeps
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:envoy OR source:traefik) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*/mcp* @network.destination.port:8080 -CIDR(@network.client.ip, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 LocalPort=8080
| ConnectionDirection=1 OR ConnectionDirection="InboundConnectionAccepted"
| ContextImageFileName=/(python3?|uvicorn|gunicorn|dockerd?|containerd)/i
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, action, protocol, bytes, packets
| filter dstPort = 8080
      and action = "ACCEPT"
      and protocol = 6
      and not (srcAddr like /^10\./)
      and not (srcAddr like /^192\.168\./)
      and not (srcAddr like /^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\./)
      and not (srcAddr like /^127\./)
| stats count(*) as flows, sum(bytes) as total_bytes by srcAddr, dstAddr
| sort flows desc
| limit 200

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| where NOT (cidrmatch("10.0.0.0/8", src) OR cidrmatch("192.168.0.0/16", src) OR cidrmatch("172.16.0.0/12", src))

| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Meta Graph API outbound carrying access_token in URL query (CVE-2026-48039) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects post-exploitation token exfiltration where meta-ads-mcp ≤ 1.0.101 leaks the operator's META_ACCESS_TOKEN via the request_url field of Graph API error responses (api.py:136 puts the token in the URL query string, and api.py:263-269 echoes it back). Pivots on outbound HTTPS to graph.facebook.com with 'access_token=' visible in the URL, with the source process correlated to the meta-ads-mcp Python runtime. Rationale: The advisory is explicit that the leaked URL has the literal substring 'access_token=' followed by the operator's META_ACCESS_TOKEN — Meta Graph API endpoint plus 'access_token=' in the query string is the article's own indicator. Cross-referenced Meta's Graph API docs (graph.facebook.com/v24.0/...) which confirm v24.0 is the current API surface used by the vulnerable code path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr • https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview
ATT&CKT1528 T1041 T1552.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Meta Marketing API integrations that still pass access_token as URL parameter (deprecated but functional)
  • Older Meta SDK versions that haven't migrated to Authorization Bearer header
  • Developer-debug calls captured by a proxy with cleartext token logging
  • Server-side analytics agents calling Graph API via query-string auth
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--debug","--trace","facebook_business_sdk"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: extract the access_token (or its prefix) from the URL, validate it against Meta Business Manager to identify which ad account / business is exposed. Confirm the source host is running meta-ads-mcp (cross-ref UC3 inventory). Step 2 — Contain: immediately invalidate the leaked META_ACCESS_TOKEN via Meta Business Settings → System Users → revoke token, then rotate. Patch meta-ads-mcp to ≥ 1.0.109 (or apply the upstream fix: move token to Authorization Bearer header per the advisory's remediation guidance). Restrict the MCP service to authenticated callers only. Step 3 — Hunt: search 90d back for the same TokenPreview being used from non-corporate IPs (attacker is now reusing it); review Meta Ads activity log for unauthorised ad-account modifications, campaign creation, or pixel-data exports; pivot to UC1 to identify the originating /mcp request and the unauthenticated caller IP.
let MCPHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
    | distinct DeviceId, DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.facebook.com"
   or RemoteUrl has "graph.fb.com"
| where DeviceId in (MCPHosts) 
   or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python.exe","python3","python","uvicorn.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationHostName has_any ("graph.facebook.com", "graph.fb.com")
   or RequestURL has_any ("graph.facebook.com", "graph.fb.com")
| where RequestURL has "access_token="
| extend RawToken = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)", 1, RequestURL)
| extend TokenPreview = substring(RawToken, 0, 12)
| extend TokenLen = strlen(RawToken)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, RequestMethod, TokenPreview, TokenLen, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:nginx OR source:envoy OR source:proxy OR source:zeek OR source:windows.sysmon) (@http.url_details.host:graph.facebook.com OR @DestinationHostname:graph.facebook.com OR @QueryName:graph.facebook.com) (@http.url:*access_token=* OR @url:*access_token=* OR @CommandLine:*access_token=*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/graph\.(facebook|fb)\.com$/i
| join({
    #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 
    | CommandLine=/meta[_-]ads[_-]mcp/i OR ImageFileName=/(python3?|uvicorn|gunicorn)/i
    | groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=count())
  }, field=aid, include=[ComputerName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(), limit=max)
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents from datamodel=Web where Web.dest="graph.facebook.com" Web.url="*access_token=*" by Web.src Web.dest Web.user 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rex field=urls "access_token=(?<token_preview>[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{0,12})"
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents from datamodel=Web where Web.dest="graph.facebook.com" Web.url="*access_token=*" by Web.src Web.dest Web.user 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rex field=urls "access_token=(?<token_preview>[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{0,12})"
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp installation hunt (CVE-2026-48039, ≤ 1.0.101) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory and process-execution hunt for pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp installations vulnerable to CVE-2026-48039, covering Python/uvicorn/gunicorn/Docker invocations of the meta_ads_mcp module, package-manager evidence, and Defender TVM software inventory entries. Prioritises versions ≤ 1.0.101 (commit 496c988 ~ 7d14226) and the unconfirmed 1.0.102–1.0.105 range. Rationale: Article names the exact module/repo (pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp, package 'meta-ads-mcp'), the affected version band (≤ 1.0.101, commit 496c988 ~ 7d14226), and the typical runtime (Docker container, Python-based FastAPI/Starlette server given Starlette-style middleware in code excerpt). Hunt grounds on those literal strings, not a generic template. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1518
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimately-deployed meta-ads-mcp ≥ 1.0.109 (patched) running as a marketing-team automation service
  • Engineering CI containers running meta-ads-mcp for integration tests
  • Developer laptops with local meta-ads-mcp clones for contribution / debugging
  • Docker image-scanning tools (Trivy, Grype) momentarily instantiating the package to read metadata
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","build-agent","ci-runner")) and not (SoftwareVersion startswith "1.0.109" or SoftwareVersion startswith "1.0.11" or SoftwareVersion startswith "1.1.")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: for each hit, capture the SoftwareVersion (from DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory) or grep the running container/venv for the package version. Confirm whether the host exposes port 8080 externally (cross-ref UC1). Step 2 — Contain: for vulnerable versions (≤ 1.0.108 per the advisory), either upgrade to ≥ 1.0.109 immediately, restrict the MCP service to localhost / internal-only network, or stop the service until patched. Rotate the host's META_ACCESS_TOKEN as a precaution. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC1 (inbound /mcp on 8080) and UC2 (Graph API access_token leak) on the same DeviceId for the last 30 days to determine whether exploitation has already occurred; check Meta Business Manager audit log for the operator account.
let ProcessHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","pipeboard","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001")
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001")
    | where FileName has_any ("python.exe","python3","python","uvicorn.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn","docker.exe","docker","dockerd.exe")
       or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python.exe","python3","python","uvicorn.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn","docker.exe","docker")
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), SampleCmd=any(ProcessCommandLine), Cmdlines=make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 25) by DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, AccountName;
let InventoryHits = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has_any ("meta-ads-mcp","meta_ads_mcp","pipeboard")
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), SoftwareName=any(SoftwareName), SoftwareVersion=any(SoftwareVersion) by DeviceId, DeviceName;
ProcessHits
| join kind=fullouter InventoryHits on DeviceId, DeviceName
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, SampleCmd, Cmdlines
| order by LastSeen desc
let ProcessHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","pipeboard","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001")
       or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001")
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), SampleCmd=any(coalesce(TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine)) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName;
let SecEventHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","pipeboard","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001")
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine) by DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername=Account, ActingProcessName=ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName=NewProcessName;
ProcessHits
| union SecEventHits
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp Module Execution (CVE-2026-48039)
id: f7c3e8b2-a1d5-4e9f-9b8c-2d4e6f8a1b3c
description: Inventory hunt - process execution of pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp via Python/uvicorn/gunicorn/Docker. Prioritise hosts running versions ≤ 1.0.101.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1518
  - cve.2026.48039
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'meta_ads_mcp'
      - 'meta-ads-mcp'
      - 'meta-ads-mcp-vuln001'
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '\uvicorn.exe'
      - '/uvicorn'
      - '/gunicorn'
      - '\docker.exe'
      - '/docker'
  condition: selection_cmd and selection_proc
falsepositives:
  - Authorised Meta Ads automation services
  - Engineering test instances of meta-ads-mcp running ≥ 1.0.109 (patched)
level: medium
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:docker) (@process.command_line:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp-vuln001*) OR @CommandLine:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp-vuln001*) OR @process.executable.path:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| CommandLine=/meta[_-]ads[_-]mcp(-vuln001)?/i OR ImageFileName=/meta[_-]ads[_-]mcp/i
| ImageFileName=/(python3?|uvicorn|gunicorn|dockerd?)/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/(python3?|uvicorn|gunicorn|dockerd?)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, UserName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_path) as binaries from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*meta_ads_mcp*" OR Processes.process="*meta-ads-mcp*" OR Processes.process="*meta-ads-mcp-vuln001*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_path) as binaries from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*meta_ads_mcp*" OR Processes.process="*meta-ads-mcp*" OR Processes.process="*meta-ads-mcp-vuln001*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
CVE-2026-48039 PoC artefact execution (poc.py, meta-ads-mcp-vuln001 image, dispatch bypass) AIExploitation High
Detects execution of the public PoC for CVE-2026-48039 — the article's reproduction recipe runs 'docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -e META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789 meta-ads-mcp-vuln001' followed by 'python3 poc.py'. Also surfaces file writes of http_auth_integration.py, api.py, or poc.py outside of legitimate development paths. Rationale: Pulls the most distinctive literal strings the article publishes in its 'Proof of Concept' block: the placeholder token 'FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789' (unique enough to be a near-zero-FP detection on its own), the Docker image tag 'meta-ads-mcp-vuln001', and the 'poc.py' filename. Any of these appearing on a managed host signals either active reproduction of the exploit or red-team / attacker dry-run. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.006 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AppSec / red team running the published PoC in a sandbox for triage
  • Security research lab detonating the GHSA reference exploit
  • Detection-engineering test harness validating this very rule
  • Vulnerability-scanner verification modules that ship the published PoC
  • Docker image-scanning tool pulling meta-ads-mcp-vuln001 to inspect layers
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","appsec-","redteam-","ci-","build-")) and not (AccountName has_any ("appsec","redteam","secresearch"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the user and host running the PoC. Determine if this is a sanctioned sandbox (compare DeviceName against the AppSec/red-team asset list) or a production-tier host. Capture the parent-process chain — docker daemon vs. an interactive shell tells you operator intent. Step 2 — Contain: if non-sandbox, isolate the host via Defender 'Isolate device'; kill the python3/docker process; remove the meta-ads-mcp-vuln001 image (`docker rmi`); preserve poc.py for forensics. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC1 (whether the PoC actually hit a real meta-ads-mcp instance — check egress to live MCP servers) and UC2 (whether a real META_ACCESS_TOKEN — not the FAKE_TOKEN_ placeholder — leaked); review the user's Git/clipboard history for the PoC source; check whether the same SHA256 of poc.py appears on other endpoints (worm-style spread of the PoC).
let ProcExec = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("poc.py","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789")
    | where FileName has_any ("python.exe","python3","python","docker.exe","docker","dockerd.exe")
       or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("docker.exe","docker","bash","sh","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256;
let FileWrite = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("poc.py","http_auth_integration.py","api.py")
    | where FolderPath has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","poc.py")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
ProcExec
| union FileWrite
| order by Timestamp desc
let ProcExec = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has_any ("poc.py","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789")
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3","python","docker.exe","docker")
       or ParentProcessName has_any ("docker.exe","docker","bash","sh","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName;
let AsimExec = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("poc.py","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789")
       or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("poc.py","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, NewProcessName=TargetProcessName, CommandLine=coalesce(TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine), ParentProcessName=ActingProcessName;
ProcExec
| union AsimExec
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Miasma supply-chain worm leaked repo clone, install or fetch · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Cybersecurity Stars Awards 2026: Winners Announced Across 95 Categories
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Miasma worm GitHub commit-search C2 magic strings on command line or script · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Miasma worm GitHub commit-search C2 magic strings on command line or script AICommand & Control High
Hunts for the three hard-coded GitHub commit-search query strings the Miasma supply-chain worm uses as its three independent C2 channels (PAT discovery, JavaScript payload delivery, Python payload delivery). These strings have zero legitimate business presence and are the highest-fidelity Miasma indicator available. Rationale: The three strings 'DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom', 'TheBeautifulSandsOfTime' and 'firedalazer' are the hard-coded GitHub commit-search queries each Miasma C2 channel uses (PAT discovery, JS payload, Python payload). They are confirmed by SafeDep's analysis, BleepingComputer's report, and a parallel TheHackerNews write-up. Zero legitimate business processes contain these tokens. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-supply-chain-attack-compromises.html • https://cloudsmith.com/blog/miasma-worms-path-of-destruction • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/09/miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit-goes-public-on-github/5253074
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.007 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst running these strings through their own grep/search tooling for hunting
  • SOC engineer pasting the IOCs into a script or note file
  • Security researcher cloning or reading SafeDep / Cloudsmith write-ups in a developer IDE that logs URL paths
  • Sandbox / detonation environment intentionally executing a Miasma sample for analysis
  • Automation that ingests OSS-supply-chain advisories and writes IOCs to a database column
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("misp.exe","opencti.exe") and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\sandbox\\","\\detonation\\","\\analyst-tools\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the process that emitted the string is not an analyst hunting tool, a CTI ingestion script, or a known sandbox. Pull the full ProcessCommandLine and parent chain; if the string was in a network URL, identify what process issued the GET against api.github.com/search/commits. 2) Contain: if the originating process is a node/python/git/curl invocation on a developer machine or CI runner, isolate the host from network, revoke any GitHub PATs and SSH keys cached on it, and rotate npm/PyPI/RubyGems publish tokens and JFrog Artifactory credentials owned by that user. 3) Hunt: search 30d for the same three strings org-wide; pivot on the parent process and SHA256 to find sibling executions; review the developer's git push history for npm/PyPI/RubyGems package versions published in the last 7d for unexpected new releases or postinstall scripts.
let MiasmaC2 = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSandsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, Source = "Process";
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","github.com")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName = InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256, Source = strcat("Net:", RemoteUrl);
union ProcHits, NetHits
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
let MiasmaC2 = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSandsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
let From4688 = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source = "4688";
let FromAsim = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName = ActingProcessName, Source = "ASIM";
union From4688, FromAsim
| where Account !endswith "$"
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Worm GitHub Commit Search C2 Magic Strings
id: a7d4e8b2-9c3f-4e1d-b8a5-7f2e9d8c4a1b
description: Detects command-line invocations containing the three GitHub commit-search C2 query strings used by the Miasma supply-chain worm (variant of Shai-Hulud) for PAT discovery, JavaScript payload delivery, and Python payload delivery.
references:
  - https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-supply-chain-attack-compromises.html

author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:

  - attack.t1102.002

      - 'DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom'

level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.defender) (@CommandLine:(*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom* OR *TheBeautifulSandsOfTime* OR *firedalazer*) OR @process.command_line:(*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom* OR *TheBeautifulSandsOfTime* OR *firedalazer*))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=SyntheticProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=ScriptControlScanInfo)
| CommandLine=/(DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom|TheBeautifulSandsOfTime|firedalazer)/i OR ScriptContent=/(DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom|TheBeautifulSandsOfTime|firedalazer)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process_name) as process_name values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom*" OR Processes.process="*TheBeautifulSandsOfTime*" OR Processes.process="*firedalazer*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Miasma supply-chain worm leaked repo clone, install or fetch AIDelivery High
Hunts for git clone / npm install / pip install / curl / wget operations that reference the briefly-public 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' GitHub repositories which leaked the worm's source on 2026-06-08. A match means the host has either ingested the leaked toolkit or is being staged with it. Rationale: 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' is the exact repository slug SafeDep and BleepingComputer report appeared on GitHub from 2026-06-08 hosting the leaked toolkit. The string is uniquely tied to Miasma and would only surface in dev-tool command lines or proxy URLs when a host is cloning, installing or downloading the leaked source. Cross-checked via SafeDep, BleepingComputer and TheRegister. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/09/miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit-goes-public-on-github/5253074 • https://cloudsmith.com/blog/miasma-worms-path-of-destruction
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1105 T1588.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal threat-intel team intentionally cloning the leaked repo into a sandbox for analysis
  • Security researcher fetching the source on a developer workstation for write-up
  • SOAR / TIP ingesting OSS advisory feeds and storing the repo URL as an IOC string
  • Vulnerability scanner or SCA tool fingerprinting against known-malicious repo names
  • Blue-team CTF or training environment seeding the toolkit deliberately
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has_any ("\\sandbox\\", "\\detonation\\", "\\malware-analysis\\", "\\threat-intel\\") and FolderPath !has_any ("\\sandbox\\", "\\detonation\\", "\\malware-analysis\\", "\\threat-intel\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user and parent process that issued the clone/install/fetch — confirm it is not a sanctioned analyst sandbox or CTI ingestion job. Pull the full ProcessCommandLine and any subsequent npm/pip postinstall script execution from the same host. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill any node/python child processes spawned within 1 hour of the clone, revoke GitHub PATs and SSH keys cached on it, and rotate npm/PyPI/RubyGems/Artifactory publish tokens belonging to the user. 3) Hunt: search 30d for the three Miasma C2 commit-search strings (see related UC) on the same host and across the org; review the user's recent package publishes for unexpected versions; check GitHub Actions workflows in any repo they touched for newly-added steps referencing untrusted secrets or external scripts.
let MiasmaRepo = "Miasma-Open-Source-Release";
let DevTools = dynamic(["git.exe","npm.exe","node.exe","pip.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","git","npm","node","pip","python","python3","curl","wget"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ (DevTools) or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (DevTools)
    | where ProcessCommandLine contains MiasmaRepo or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains MiasmaRepo
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, Source = "Process";
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl contains MiasmaRepo
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "Network";
union isfuzzy=true ProcHits, NetHits
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
let MiasmaRepo = "Miasma-Open-Source-Release";
let From4688 = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine contains MiasmaRepo
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source = "4688";
let FromAsim = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine contains MiasmaRepo or TargetProcessCommandLine contains MiasmaRepo
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName = ActingProcessName, Source = "ASIM";
let FromProxy = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL contains MiasmaRepo or DestinationHostName contains MiasmaRepo
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = SourceHostName, Account = SourceUserName, NewProcessName = "", CommandLine = RequestURL, ParentProcessName = "", Source = "Proxy";
union From4688, FromAsim, FromProxy
| where Account !endswith "$"
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
